correctness.rationale: The exact burning condition for every stable K_{2,n} configuration admits 2k+1 recurrent hub pairs for k occupied nonsink leaves. Explicit legal stabilization separates zero, intermediate, maximal cases for both source orbits; summing yields both displayed all-n polynomial identities, each n*2^(n-1) states. The intermediate coefficients are binomial and their combined probability exactly 1/n, so the weak limit and moments follow analytically. Executable independent enumeration checks every stable state for n=2..10 and coefficients for n=2..512, but those computations are only corroboration. Source can topple twice in the maximum leaf case, captured in proof.

value.rationale: The object K_{2,n} is the smallest nontrivial two-hub complete bipartite sandpile; its source dependence is a natural finite-size diagnostic. The theorem determines the complete probability law for both inequivalent drive sites, beyond known extremal coefficients and moments. The all-or-none system-spanning law coexists with a rare O(1/n) binomially concentrated bridge at half size. For a leaf source the maximal event has precisely one doubly toppled vertex, giving a distinct wave structure. Such an exact classification is a meaningful reference case for avalanche distributions and is not just a substitution or isolated invariant; no unsupported universality is claimed.
